transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-05 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Diego Morales (Redwood CSM), Marta Li (Harborline Procurement), Samir Gupta (Harborline SRE), Elaine Park (Harborline Legal), Tom Reyes (Harborline PM)

Summary: short intake to surface procurement and security requirements for onboarding Redwood inference; confirm SLA/KMS/SSO needs, pricing approval path, and pilot technical owners.

Topics: MSA/DPA redlines, SLA tiers and uptime/latency targets, KMS & keying options, VPC/private deployment vs hosted, pricing/commit commitments, pilot success criteria, next steps and owners.

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining uh we'll keep to 45 minutes to an hour. quick intros?
[00:12] Marta Li: hi this is Marta, head of procurement at Harborline. main reason we're on is vendor onboarding cadence and contract path.
[00:20] Samir Gupta: Samir — infra, we'll look after the pilot and perf tests.
[00:25] Elaine Park: Elaine, legal. we'll be looking at DPA and MSA redlines.
[00:30] Tom Reyes: Tom here, product. interested in latency and cost tradeoffs.
[00:34] Priya Patel: Priya, I'm Redwood SE; I'll lead the pilot and technical scope.
[00:38] Diego Morales: Diego CSM — I'll help with onboarding timing.

[02:10] Alex Chen: high level — Redwood offers hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, or private VPC/on-prem bundle. Marta, can you say which procurement lane you expect? is this straight hosted buy or do you need dedicated/reserved?
[02:25] Marta Li: procurement prefers managed hosted for speed but Finance may push for reserved capacity if cost savings are clear. we need pricing scenarios for both. also, governance needs from Elaine — DPA and SOC 2 are must-haves.

[04:05] Elaine Park: yes SOC 2 Type II and ISO are table stakes. also we need audit log retention details, data residency for eu traffic, and a clear KMS story — do you support customer-managed keys?
[04:18] Priya Patel: short answer: yes we have KMS integrations (customer-managed KMS in our Private offering), for Hosted we offer BYOK via partner KMS and for Dedicated there's an option to bring your own keying. note: some wording in our DPA about ephemeral caching might need clarity, we can provide the cryptography whitepaper. (small pause) sorry — cryptography whitepaper, and HSM options.

[06:00] Samir Gupta: okay — for pilot we probably want to run both Hosted and Dedicated comparison, 5k QPS burst, and p95 target around 200ms for our chat assistant flows, p99 less critical but we'd like to see numbers. how much control over model variants during failover?
[06:20] Priya Patel: we support routing policies — latency-first or cost-first — and automatic fallback to compatible model quantized variants; can pin versions per-route. we'll include runbook showing routes and fallback behavior.

[08:10] Tom Reyes: when you say dedicated, what is the provisioning lead time and SLA? procurement needs an SLA table to map to our acceptance criteria.
[08:22] Alex Chen: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with SLA-backed uptime, typical provisioning 2–4 weeks depending on region and GPU type; SLA tiers we can share — uptime, latency thresholds, MTTR, maintenance windows. we'll send the SLA matrix.

[10:15] Elaine Park: on the MSA, we have three common asks: limited liability cap alignment to our standard, data classification language for customer data, and explicit egress costs for EU/eus residency. who handles data residency guarantees?
[10:33] Alex Chen: redwood has region pinning and private deployments; for strict residency we recommend our Private deployment or a dedicated VPC with customer-managed control plane. I can share the standard residency clause and a variant we've used.

[12:00] Marta Li: procurement timeline — we aim to finalize commercial terms by end of Q3; we need a pricing approval sheet for Finance by 6/15 to get early buy-in. can you provide committed spend vs on-demand examples?
[12:12] Priya Patel: yes — we'll produce tiers: pay-as-you-go hosted, monthly reserved capacity with discount bands, and pilot discount. we'll include an example showing cost per 1M tokens at various batch sizes and quantization settings.

[14:05] Samir Gupta: security-wise we need SSO integration (SAML/SCIM) and RBAC, plus audit logs for token-level events. do you support token-level tracing in the console?
[14:18] Diego Morales: (interjects) we do have per-token cost breakdown in Console and token-level tagging for traced requests, though exact retention windows vary by plan.
[14:30] Priya Patel: we'll list retention windows; for enterprise we can extend log retention via archive. SCIM + SAML support yes, and RBAC with role bindings is available.

[16:40] Elaine Park: DPA question: we need standard subprocessors list and a commitment on notification for changes. also, encryption in transit + at rest is required, and can you commit to key rotation policy visibility?
[17:00] Priya Patel: subprocessors list we'll provide; notifications are in our DPA template. encryption in transit and at rest yes; key rotation depends on KMS — for BYOK we surface rotation events. we'll attach the subprocessor registry link. (mumble: link sent after)

[19:10] Tom Reyes: on latencies — what's the expected tail latency impact when using quantized models vs full precision? we want to understand accuracy regressions and cost wins.
[19:25] Priya Patel: quantization typically reduces memory and can improve throughput but may slightly affect token prediction quality; we'll provide benchmark artifacts for the model family you plan to run and suggested eval prompt sets. we'll note quality delta metrics.

[21:00] Marta Li: procurement also flagged export controls and whether any of your GPU stack involves restricted tech; need a short statement for compliance.
[21:14] Alex Chen: we can provide an export controls statement; our legal has a template we've used for other financials. we'll include a simple one-page attestation.

[23:00] Samir Gupta: for pilot environment, do we get isolated tenancy? we prefer not to mix with general multi-tenant for bridging PII.
[23:14] Priya Patel: for Dedicated you get isolated GPU pools and we can enable prefix/KV cache partitioning; for Private, you can have full private control plane in your VPC. I'll outline options and recommended configuration for PII minimization.

[25:30] Elaine Park: about indemnities — our counsel will likely ask for a narrower indemnity carveout for data breaches caused by your gross negligence; do you have standard language?
[25:47] Alex Chen: we have precedent clauses; we typically balance liability with SLA credits and caps. we'll share the clause we've negotiated previously and note which parts are negotiable.

[28:00] Tom Reyes: Tom here — on the pilot success criteria: we need throughput >= 2k sustained for 95% of windows, average p95 latency < 400ms under our traffic, and regression on model outputs under 2% measured by our eval set. can Redwood run regression checks?
[28:18] Priya Patel: yes, Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. for the pilot we'll run both performance and quality evals and share dashboards.

[30:00] Diego Morales: timeline recap: we'll aim for a two-week pilot setup after legal sign-off; tech kickoff week of 6/15, duration 3 weeks, then decision go/no-go for reserved capacity.

[32:40] Marta Li: procurement question — are you open to a short-term pilot MOA (memorandum of agreement) for the pilot terms rather than full MSA to accelerate testing?
[32:55] Alex Chen: yes we typically use a pilot addendum or short MOA to cover liabilities and pilot constraints; we'll share a template.

[34:10] Elaine Park: please include an escalation contact list and a security questionnaire — our InfoSec will send an 80-question vendor security survey. will Redwood fill that out?
[34:22] Priya Patel: we'll complete the security questionnaire; for anything long we'll invite our security lead to a follow-up meeting.

[36:00] Samir Gupta: one more technical: do you allow bringing custom models or only hosted model catalog? we may have internal models we want to run.
[36:15] Priya Patel: supported — Dedicated and Private both allow customer model onboarding; hosted may allow containerized model upload for enterprise tiers. we'll include the model onboarding checklist.

[38:20] Tom Reyes: what about network egress costs and measurement? Finance wants clear egress line items per GB for EU to US traffic.
[38:35] Alex Chen: egress is tracked and billed separately; we'll provide the egress table and examples. for Private deployments, egress might be internal to your VPC so different.

[40:00] Marta Li: ok good. on approvals, who will sign the MSA? do you need a procurement PO or just signature?
[40:12] Diego Morales: we accept both; for enterprise we typically generate an invoice and can accept PO numbers. we'll list billing paths.

[42:05] Elaine Park: small nit — in your DPA there was a line referencing 'KV cache persistence' that legal misread as long-term storage; please clarify that it's in-memory cache and short TTL unless explicitly configured.
[42:20] Priya Patel: good catch — the note should say ephemeral KV cache with configurable TTL; we'll send the exact language and update the DPA template.

[44:00] Alex Chen: quick recap of deliverables: MSA/DPA examples and redline suggestions (Alex), SLA matrix (Alex), pilot runbook + benchmark spreadsheets (Priya), security questionnaire response plan (Priya/Diego), and Harborline to share traffic profile and decision timeline (Samir/Marta).

[44:30] Marta Li: timeline — we'll review docs internally and aim to have procurement feedback by 6/15; legal may need until 6/22 for DPA redlines.

[46:10] Tom Reyes: any blockers on our side for the pilot? Samir we need infra access and sample data scrubbed.
[46:22] Samir Gupta: yes we'll prepare scrubbed dataset and a service account for access.

[48:00] Elaine Park: we'll also need to see your SOC 2 report and subprocessor list.
[48:10] Alex Chen: we'll attach SOC 2 Type II report and subprocessor registry.

[50:00] Diego Morales: final housekeeping — how do you prefer we share docs? slack channel + email plus a shared drive; I'll set up a channel if you want.
[50:12] Marta Li: slack channel good, and please cc procurement inbox.

[51:00] Alex Chen: perfect thanks everyone. we'll get these artifacts out this week. thanks Harborline, look forward to pilot.

Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: there are occasional stutters and mis-heard proper nouns (e.g., K-V cash for KV cache), some speaker labels consolidated.
